### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #39929

Problem Summary:

The problem is that a pessimistic txn never locks a non-unique index key, and then the DDL merge worker only writes to the index key. These two txns are not aware of each other. For details, see #39929.

### What is changed and how it works?

- Lock the row keys when merging back from the temp index.
- Add the temp index value format:
  - `[delete_flag] [handle] [temp_key_ver]`
  - `[normal_flag] [origin_index_value] [temp_key_ver]`
- Add a unit test for temp index value codec and a integration test for key locking.

issue_context.title: Pessimistic lock not found during adding index
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks! ### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required) It is not easy to reproduce because it requires the retry of a prewrite request.
Row Index Temp Index Index state Txn 1: DDL Txn 2: pessimistic Txn 0: DML
1 write-only update a = 2 where id = 1
2 1d, 2 write-only
2 1d, 2 Write-reorg

backfill

2 2 1d, 2 Write-reorg

merge

2 2 1d, 2 Write-reorg

merge

Begin

Update a = 3 where id = 1

(2 -> 3)

2 2 1d, 2 Write-reorg

merge

Begin

Read temp index and write index

(1d, 2)

commit

2 1

2

1d, 2 Write-reorg

merge

commit
3 1

2

2

3

For pessimistic txn, write conflicts are converted to “pessimistic lock not found”

1d, 2d, 3
Note: "1d" means a DML txn deletes the index key "1", it is converted to "1 -> deleted" and only stored by the temp index. ### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required) The DDL should be blocked by the pessimistic lock. ### 3. What did you see instead (Required) The DDL and DML successfully executed. ### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required) bb50e33509

review_comments: why here set mdl lock disable?
DDL will be blocked by MDL definitely if we activate a txn in `tk2`.
Why here need TempIndexKeyState public outside of the package?

Because exported functions should not have the unexported return type.

```
func KeyExistInTempIndex(ctx context.Context, txn kv.Transaction, key kv.Key, distinct bool, h kv.Handle, IsCommonHandle bool) (tempIndexKeyState, kv.Handle, error) {
```
